title: On the Realizability of Edge-Girth Sequences
summary: The edge-girth of an edge $e$ in a simple connected graph is the length of a shortest cycle containing $e$, with $g_e = \infty$ if no such cycle exists, and the edge-girth sequence of a graph is the nondecreasing sequence of the edge-girths of its edges. We characterize the sequences that are realizable as the edge-girth sequence of a simple connected graph. A constant sequence $(g^{(m)})$ with $g$ finite and $m \geq 1$ is realizable if and only if $m = g$ or $m \geq \lceil 3g/2 \rceil$.
